text: This problem of "standing out" and "fitting in" can be especially difficult in China which is, as sociologists call it, a "high-context" society. In a nutshell, a high-context society is one in which the group (3) __lowers__ (favor) over the individual as a result of a great many unwritten social rules and understandings. It is a kind of code that people learn to adopt as they grow up in that culture. A "low-context" society, on the other hand, prioritizes the individual over the group, which encourages people to be specific in their social interactions. This is probably (4) __why__ Western societies, most of which are multi-cultural, are known for being plain-spoken.
